title: 1968 AHSME Problem 33
statement: A number \(N\) has three digits when expressed in base \(7.\) When \(N\) is expressed in base \(9\) the digits are reversed. Then the middle digit is:

solutions.text:
Let \(N=(abc)_7=(cba)_9.\) Then \(49a+7b+c=81c+9b+a,\) so \(24a-b=40c.\) With \(1\leq a\leq6,\) \(0\leq b\leq6,\) and \(1\leq c\leq6,\) the only possibility is \(a=5,\) \(c=3,\) \(b=0.\) Indeed, \((503)_7=(305)_9=248.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
